rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3, two-year field experiment (2018-2020) in Yuanyang County with FI, DI and RF under three cropping systems, measured SWC, SNC, LAI, DM and yields, plus WHCNS model calibrated/validated on these. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 7, DI irrigated 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y received 34%, 36% and 40% less irrigation than FI over two years (water meters recorded amounts) while yields were maintained or higher; seasonal water saving 31% for wheat and 40% for maize. Q4: Table 7 and Section 3.3, model simulated the intermediate water-loss terms (soil evaporation lower by 8-74%, drainage by 61-74%, runoff by 37-49% under DI), and SWC was measured at 0-100 cm (Fig. 2). Q8: Section 4.4, authors state drainage, ET, runoff were not measured so simulated water fates carry large uncertainty, and that more observed datasets would be needed for calibration.
rows.notes: The 34/36/40% figures in the study refer to the 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y cropping systems, not to wheat vs maize as the passage phrases it; the water saving is essentially the designed difference in applied irrigation amounts (Eq. 6), with the result being that yields were not reduced. Q3 no: a single site experiment plus a model calibrated on the same data is not two independent methods. Q5 no: one site, one soil, effectively two crop species (wheat and maize). Q6 no: 96 m2 plots. Q7 no: discussion attributes savings to small frequent applications but cites other work; no condition stated as a requirement from own findings. Q9 no: no dispersion reported for irrigation savings or water balance terms (Table 7), although WUE in Table 6 carries +/- values.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3, two-year replicated field experiment with measured grain yields. Q2: Section 3.2, Table 6, Fig. 4, DI 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y total grain yields of 39829, 29619 and 21777 kg/ha versus 36962, 29542 and 21290 kg/ha under FI; order of yields DI > FI > RF. Q4: Fig. 2 and Section 4.1, soil water content measured at 0-100 cm and authors report FI produced excess SWC while DI kept SWC near optimum; LAI and DM also measured. Q8: Section 4.4, limited measured datasets for calibration and large uncertainties in simulated crop yields. Q9: Table 6, grain yields reported with +/- values (e.g. 8933+/-173 vs 8273+/-192 kg/ha for winter wheat).
rows.notes: Internal inconsistency: Section 3.2 states no significant difference between DI and FI under the same cropping system but then reports a significant difference and DI > FI order; Table 6 letters indicate DI > FI. Yield gains are modest (2-8%). Q3 no: measured and simulated yields are not independent since the model was calibrated on the measured yields. Q5 no: one site/soil, wheat and maize only. Q6 no: plot scale. Q7 no: no stated conditions for the yield effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.4, field experiment plus WHCNS model. Q2: Section 3.4 and Table 8, simulated annual N leaching 58-62% lower under DI than FI (e.g. 46.5 vs 111.7 kg/ha for 2H1Y); Table 6, NUE significantly higher under DI (32.1 vs 26.5 kg/kg for 2H1Y); the model was validated against measured soil mineral N at 0-100 cm (Fig. 3, Table 3) and yields from the same plots. Q4: Table 7 and Fig. 2, drainage simulated (74%/61%/69% lower under DI) and soil water content and soil mineral N profiles measured, i.e. the pathway from drip to reduced leaching. Q8: Section 4.4, authors explicitly state N leaching, volatilization and denitrification were not measured, so simulated N fates carry large uncertainties.
rows.notes: N leaching values are model outputs only; they were never directly measured, though the model was checked against measured soil mineral N and water content from the same system (moderate accuracy, nRMSE 15-30% for SNC). The causal direction in the passage (leaching reduced because NUE improved) is asserted in the discussion, not tested. Q3 no: single modelling approach. Q5 no: one site. Q6 no: plot scale. Q7 no: no requirement stated from own findings. Q9 no: Table 8 N-fate values carry no dispersion; only NUE in Table 6 has +/- values.

notes: Full text available including methods, results, discussion and limitations section. Key caveat for all rows: water-balance components (evaporation, drainage, runoff) and N fates (leaching, volatilization, denitrification) are WHCNS simulations not measured in the field; irrigation amounts, SWC, SNC, LAI, DM and yields were measured. Single site, two years, 96 m2 plots.
